scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8879: Users in both pods report that no internal portal
loads by NAME anymore -- web0.local through web3.local all fail with
name-resolution errors. Loading a portal directly by its IP address (e.g.
http://10.200.0.3) still works, and pings to 10.200.0.2 succeed. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dns_server BIND (named) DNS service
Mechanism: the named daemon on dns_server (10.200.0.2) has been killed, so
  nothing answers on port 53 and every *.local lookup from the pods times
  out -- which is why the portals fail by name. Everything else is healthy:
  the host 10.200.0.2 itself is up and pingable, the OSPF path works, and
  the web servers keep serving HTTP (portals load when addressed by IP).
  The symptom is purely dead name resolution.
Localization: dns_server
Root cause: named not running on dns_server (port 53 closed)
Fix: `systemctl start named` on dns_server
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`).
Once named is answering again, web0.local..web3.local resolve to their
10.200.0.x addresses and the portals load by name. The web servers and the
network need no change.

bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken

agent.diagnosis_text:
The BIND9 DNS daemon (`named`) on `dns_server` (10.200.0.2) was completely stopped at the time of the user report — port 53 returned "connection refused" to every query. Both host pods configure `nameserver 10.200.0.2` in `/etc/resolv.conf`, so every name lookup for `web0.local`–`web3.local` hit the dead daemon and failed with an immediate transport error, while direct-IP traffic and ICMP to 10.200.0.2 continued to work normally through the underlying routing fabric (OSPF/static routes are unaffected).

The BIND zone configuration itself is entirely correct: `named-checkconf` exits 0, and `db.local` contains valid A records mapping `web0`–`web3` to `10.200.0.3`–`10.200.0.6`. Manually launching `named -u bind -c /etc/bind/named.conf` immediately restored service — all four names resolved in the same diagnostic session, confirming the zone data was never the problem.

The root cause is a missing Kathara device startup script. No `/startup` file or `/etc/kathara.d/` entry exists on `dns_server` to launch `named` when the lab container initialises. The `named.service` unit is marked `enabled` in systemd but never activated (Kathara containers do not go through a full systemd boot sequence), so the daemon is absent every time the lab is started from scratch.

**Corrective fix:** Add a `dns_server.startup` file to the Kathara lab directory containing `service named start` (or `named -u bind -c /etc/bind/named.conf`). This ensures BIND launches automatically on every lab start. No zone-file or routing changes are required.

Adding a Kathara startup script to run/restore named will start BIND (and ensure it runs on lab start), which corrects the reported DNS outage as expected.

The log shows the named daemon was inactive and port 53 refused queries; config and zones are valid and manually starting named restored DNS — the agent's conclusion that the service was not running (and that no Kathara startup script existed) is well supported.
